examples.label: Unreachable rules
examples.purpose: Symbols unreachable from the start symbol are removed by cleanup.

examples.label: Unproductive nonterminals
examples.purpose: Nonterminals that derive no terminal string are removed.

examples.label: Both issues
examples.purpose: Removing unproductive symbols can leave others unreachable, so the order matters.

examples.label: Single nullable
examples.purpose: One ε-production: the nullable symbol becomes optional wherever it appears.

examples.label: Multiple nullable
examples.purpose: Several nullable symbols in one rule: every combination of omissions must be added.

examples.label: Start nullable
examples.purpose: The start symbol derives ε, so the language contains the empty string.

examples.label: Simple unit
examples.purpose: A single unit production A → B is replaced by B's own rules.

examples.label: Unit chain
examples.purpose: A chain of unit productions A → B → C: the unit pairs are transitive.

examples.label: Arithmetic (units)
examples.purpose: The expression grammar's E → T and T → F are unit productions in disguise.

examples.label: Long rules
examples.purpose: Right-hand sides longer than two symbols must be split into binary rules.

examples.label: Mixed — all issues
examples.purpose: ε-, unit and long productions together: the whole conversion in one grammar.

examples.label: Expression grammar
examples.purpose: A realistic grammar taken all the way to Chomsky normal form.

examples.label: Balanced parentheses
examples.purpose: Terminals inside longer rules and a nullable start symbol in one grammar.
text: // Terminals inside longer rules and a nullable start symbol

examples.label: Palindromes
examples.purpose: Short and long rules mixed, with single terminals and ε as alternatives.
text: // Short and long rules mixed; ε and single terminals as alternatives
S -> a S a | b S b | a | b | eps

examples.label: Direct recursion
examples.purpose: A → Aα: the standard rewrite moves the tail into a new nonterminal.

examples.label: Indirect recursion
examples.purpose: Recursion through another nonterminal (S → A a, A → S c): substitute first, then remove it.

examples.label: Multiple NTs
examples.purpose: Several left-recursive nonterminals: the expression grammar prepared for top-down parsing.

examples.label: Regular expressions
examples.purpose: Three left-recursive layers (union, concatenation, postfix): the rewrite gives the LL-ready form.

examples.label: Sentences with an adjective list
examples.purpose: Left recursion in the adjective list: the rewrite moves it into a tail nonterminal, keeping the long names.

examples.label: Pascal excerpt (declarations)
examples.purpose: Many left-recursive lists and nullable parts in one grammar: a longer run of the transformations.
